Perfect. This app is 13 years old, hasn’t been updated in 5, and it’s a completely finished product. It has way more information hidden away on it than you’d expect, with three books one of which dates back to 1888. Seriously. 

The card images are as good as they come, the descriptions are detailed but brief in the best way possible, and whatever method of randomness they use is as random to me as shuffling a real deck of 78 cards.

At the very least it’s a perfect learning tool for how to do tarot and the cards themselves, and it works surprisingly well with readings directly pulled on the app. 

If you’re interested in tarot the history, the meanings of the cards, improvement of reading skills, this is the app for you. 

Plus, no subscription! You pay money and you have the thing you paid for, what a wild concept, huh?

reviews.text:
All You Could Ever Ask For. This tarot app is the simplest, most straightforward and streamlined app of it’s kind available on the App Store. 

It has a full catalog of interpretations for each card in the RWS. I disagree with a lot of them, or to put it better my interpretations are often different then the ones provided, but they still serve as a good jumping points. 
You can choose from a number of different spreads or go completely freeform. You can also virtually shuffle and cut the deck, which adds to the overall experience. 
Each spread is stored in your journal, which you can type up your detailed interpretations of the spread in a simple text note. There’s also the option of labeling each spread with a specific question. 

There’s a large assortment of back drops to choose from, which is a neat feature. 

Overall, this app is the best app out there to read and journal tarot readings with. I own 17 different physical tarot and oracle decks, but lately I’ve been finding myself enjoying using this app and keeping it all contained in my phone. It’s just so easy, and can be done anywhere anytime without drawing attention. I use it while riding in the car, or while waiting for food. 

And there’s no ads! It’s a godsend. Such a great app for free with no ads. You can’t beat it. 

So yeah, 5/5 stars all around. 

Future feature idea: custom meanings for each card. It would be handy to have a catalog of personalized meanings for each card.

reviews.text:
Probably the best Tarot app out there. This is overall a great app for Tarot. Many different spreads (& a custom option) make this an easy pick. They have many different versions of this same app albeit with different decks, so if the old classic standby of Rider-Waite doesn't suit you, there's many other options for you.

The customer support is also good (they can take a few weeks to get back to you, so be patient). They at least acknowledge issues & ultimately fix them, which is more than I can say of many developers, including top tier ones. Kudos for transparency on the developer's part. It's had some bugs here & there (see below or negative reviews), but as of 2.18 it seems they've all been patched.

2.18 :
Fixes all the below issues. Devs : Thanks for addressing the journal not opening.

2.17 : 
Fixes the full text issue, but now the journal is inaccessible & drops the app back to the desktop. 

2.16 :
The previous version worked perfectly, even fixing a long-standing issue with the journal becoming corrupted. 

This version is buggy & trying to tap "full text from the book" usually doesn't work if the card started as full screen. Tapping on it brings up the text but then the "full text" link becomes inaccessible. The app goes into a state where you're interacting with some interface layer *above* the text rather than the text itself. The only workaround I've found is to set the default view for readings to be text & card rather than full screen card which creates the issue above. The previous version did NOT have this bug (yes, I've confirmed on an older phone).

I'd be happy to restore an otherwise deserved full 5 star rating, but not until this issue is fixed. It makes a normally great app very aggravating to use. Buyer beware!

Comprehensive. I've used many apps of many kinds and never felt compelled to write a review, regardless of how much I enjoyed the app. I feel like I should offer my opinion on this one, though. This app has features that make it perfect for anyone learning Tarot. It has two full length Tarot guide books built into the app, explanations of over a dozen spreads, and customizable draw features (you can toggle "reversed cards" on and off in the settings, for example). The deck built into the app is the classic Rider-Waite iteration. I appreciate this fact for the easy approach to the symbolism behind each individual card - there are many informational resources regarding this version of the deck. 
My personal favorite feature of this app is probably the "Card of the Day" feature. It's designed to introduce you to a new card each day, allowing you to familiarize yourself with the major and minor arcana, gradually. Focusing or meditating on one card a day is a comfortable pace to learn a practice as intricate as Tarot.
I can't recommend this app for its own divination uses. Its interface is intuitive and fluid. Its design could have a little more personality, though. However my real reason for not recommending it for conducting readings itself has to do with my own purism. Personally, I believe a spiritual reflection like divination needs a physical aspect to ground the ensuing musings to relevant energies. But because this is only a personal preference of mine, I can't dock points on that note. I would instead recommend its use as a mobile reference source.
All things considered, I think at its price, this app is a steal for all of the material packed so neatly into it.
